source_snapshot.procedure: Copied Power Restore Policy matrix: OOB 00h/06h values 00h/01h/02h, Get Chassis Status, BMC cold reset, then manually remove/restore AC from on/off states.
source_snapshot.criteria: Policy bits and AC-return behavior must match always-off, last-state and always-on.
source_snapshot.deepseek: PARTIAL; proposes unsupported raw 00h/2Ch without an interval payload and leaves result to the user.
source_snapshot.gpt_v2: REQUIRES PACKAGE / USER CONFIRMATION for standard 00h/0Bh with approved interval/readback/timing/recovery, while excluding the copied policy body.

old_problem: The historical review left this identity Pending because the interval title, copied restore-policy body and DeepSeek 2Ch suggestion name three incompatible operations. Official IPMI 2.0 resolves the standard interval and policy commands. Instead of selecting one fragment and dropping the other, the Review layer can preserve the complete source as two explicitly separated coverage lanes with different stimuli, oracles, safety approvals and restoration.
disposition_reason: Lane A validates the title with optional Chassis 00h/0Bh, an approved nonzero seconds value, one separately authorized Chassis Control power cycle, independent OFF-to-ON timing and complete OS-ready recovery, then restores the authoritative baseline interval. Lane B preserves the copied Procedure/Criteria as four manual AC-return outcomes for 00h/06h policies, including BMC cold-reset persistence and final policy restoration. The two lanes never substitute for one another, 2Ch is rejected, all physical AC handling is operator-owned, and the immutable source contradiction remains recorded.
decision_basis: Master XLSX rows 1182-1187, exact same-row DeepSeek, exact GPT second review, tests.json, tests_gpt_merged, manifest and historical V3.1 record were directly read. The code occurs once in tests.json. The next formal identity was independently verified from queue, manifest and XLSX as row 1203 / variant 5338dfc250a92832.

Rows 1184 and 1185 have the same three-policy Procedure/Criteria, but row 1184 is the dedicated OOB Power Restore Policy identity while row 1185 Items/Script say Power Cycle Interval. The IB analogues at rows 1057/1058 show the same pair and copied-body defect; all four Source Keys remain distinct.

IPMI v2.0 section 28.9 and Table 28-10 define optional Set Power Cycle Interval as Chassis NetFn 00h/Cmd 0Bh with one [7:0] seconds byte, 1-based, 00h meaning no delay. The interval is non-volatile and governs the powered-down time for Chassis Control or watchdog power-cycle operations.

IPMI supplies no standard Get Power Cycle Interval command. Therefore a completion code alone cannot prove the stored value or safe restoration. Execution requires an authoritative BASE_INTERVAL from a Project recipe or vendor read API, a validated nonzero TEST_INTERVAL, and either target readback or separately approved functional timing evidence for both test and restored states.

The test interval is observed only through one explicitly authorized Chassis Control 00h/02h data 02h power cycle from an ON system. ED-29 requires the complete OFF, ON and OS Ready transitions; the specific off-duration tolerance is Project-owned because the standard supplies units but no acceptance tolerance.

IPMI v2.0 section 28.8 and Table 28-9 separately define Set Power Restore Policy as 00h/06h values 000b always-off, 001b previous-state, 010b always-on and 011b no-change/support query. It is non-volatile and Get Chassis Status returns the current policy; this is not interval coverage.

The copied policy Procedure requires BMC cold reset plus physical loss/restoration of the main AC feed. Its behavioral coverage has four outcome branches: always-off from ON, previous-state from ON, previous-state from OFF and always-on from OFF. Each branch needs its own starting-state and post-return evidence; one policy cannot stand for the matrix.

A BMC cold reset, an IPMI chassis power cycle and physical AC loss are different operations and timelines. They are logged separately and never described as equivalent warm/cold/AC/DC cycles. The source says AC, so a DC-feed substitution is an explicit project coverage change, not silent equivalence.

Physical cord/PDU isolation and any manual cable action remain operator-owned. Automation may issue only separately approved OOB setters/reads and collect synchronized power/BMC/OS evidence; this makes the full union MANUAL ONLY even though parts are scriptable.

DeepSeek's 00h/2Ch is rejected: it is not the IPMI Set Power Cycle Interval command and supplies no payload/schema. The generic command-line password is also replaced by host-verified secret-safe LANPlus handling.

The Source Conflict remains because the Master still labels row 1185 Interval while its body tests Policy. Pending can be removed without altering Master by requiring both lanes; any project running only one lane must report the other as uncovered and cannot PASS this full Source Key.

ED-02/ED-21/ED-26 preserve all duplicate Source Keys; ED-03/ED-13 prohibit guessed OEM behavior; ED-15/ED-18 prohibit success-only or invented thresholds; ED-17 preserves evidence and manual hardware ownership; ED-24 retains source conflicts; ED-28/ED-30 require recovery/approval; ED-29 requires OFF to ON to OS Ready; ED-33/ED-34 preserve Master while allowing bounded parameters; ED-38 prohibits automatic retry.

test_case.test_name: OOB Power Cycle Interval timing plus preserved AC Power Restore Policy behavior matrix
test_case.purpose: Preserve and independently verify both functions present in the source: configure one OOB power-cycle interval and measure its actual OFF duration through a complete controlled cycle, then exercise the copied three-value AC restore-policy matrix with physical AC handling, restoring both non-volatile settings and healthy OS state.
required_package: Dedicated non-production SUT/BMC/firmware, single-DUT AC feed map, quiesced workload/filesystems, independent KVM/serial/BMC/PDU observers, recovery-capable operator and maintenance window

Authoritative BASE_INTERVAL plus optional-command support, approved nonzero TEST_INTERVAL in seconds, target-supported range, Project timing tolerance, vendor readback if available and exact restore method
Original power-restore policy, 00h/06h support mask and Get Chassis Status policy-bit parser, cold-reset reconnect bound and four separately approved AC behavior trials
Pinned secret-safe host-verified LANPlus tool with exact 00h/0Bh, 00h/06h, 00h/01h and one-shot 00h/02h data 02h handling; retries disabled and timestamps from synchronized clocks

Qualified human procedure for identifying/removing/restoring only the DUT AC cord or controlled outlet, minimum de-energized proof/dwell, electrical safety, no shared-feed impact and independent bring-up/recovery
test_case.test_command: MANUAL POWER TEST; DO NOT EXECUTE DURING REVIEW. Capture/hash BMC/firmware, BASE_INTERVAL authority/readback, original restore policy/support, host/OS state, exact AC feed map and SEL/BMC/OS/PDU evidence without clearing logs. Lane A: validate 0Bh support, TEST_INTERVAL and tolerance; display raw 00 0b TEST plus expected OFF interval and recovery, obtain immediate approval, send once via secret-safe OOB and require completion 00h/readback if available. From confirmed OS Ready/ON, separately confirm and send one Chassis Control 00 02 02 power-cycle request. Do not retry. Independent observers must timestamp power removed, power asserted, POST and OS Ready; compare only OFF duration to TEST_INTERVAL tolerance, then verify host/filesystem/device health. Restore BASE_INTERVAL once and prove it through vendor readback or a separately authorized baseline cycle. Lane B: start only after Lane A recovery. Use 00 06 03 and 00 01 to capture support/current policy. For each isolated trial—always-off from ON, previous-state from ON, previous-state from OFF, always-on from OFF—set the exact 06h value once, verify support/current bits, perform one separately confirmed BMC cold reset, reconnect within bound and verify persistence. A qualified operator then removes only the mapped AC feed, proves full de-energization, observes the approved dwell and restores AC once. Verify the expected OFF or complete ON-to-OS-Ready result. Restore the original policy after the matrix and reverify. Keep row 1184 policy, row 1058 IB interval and every physical/power action as separate evidence; never send 2Ch.
test_case.expected_result: Lane A accepts one standard 0Bh value, retains it across the applicable non-volatile context, and one authorized Chassis Control cycle exhibits a measured OFF interval within the Project-approved tolerance followed by ON, POST and OS Ready with healthy state; BASE_INTERVAL is restored and verified. Lane B reports supported policy values, retains each selected policy across BMC cold reset, and produces four correct AC-return outcomes: off under always-off, on/off matching previous state, and on under always-on, with OS Ready whenever ON is expected. The original policy is restored and no unrelated configuration/evidence changes. Neither lane alone completes this Source Key.
test_case.pass_fail_basis: PASS requires both lanes, exact OOB target identity, official 0Bh/06h payloads, authoritative baselines, explicit per-action approvals, independent timestamped transition evidence, full OFF-to-ON-to-OS-Ready for interval/on outcomes, four policy branches, and verified restoration of interval, policy and host health. FAIL covers wrong/2Ch command, completion-only interval acceptance, out-of-tolerance OFF duration, missing transition, policy-bit/behavior mismatch, shared-feed impact, BMC reconnect failure, unexpected host damage or failed restore. NOT READY covers missing baseline/readback authority, optional-command support, tolerance, isolated feed/operator, recovery, credentials or approvals. N/A for Lane A requires target-authoritative proof that optional 0Bh is unsupported; the copied policy lane remains separately reportable and cannot convert the full union to PASS.
safety_gate: Use one isolated non-production SUT with confirmed single-DUT feed and independent console/PDU recovery. Quiesce workload and filesystems; never interrupt a shared rack feed, storage service or production node.
Do not clear logs. Preserve pre-action SEL, BMC, OS, filesystem, device and power evidence so each reset/cycle/AC loss can be correlated and first-failure evidence cannot be overwritten.
Power Cycle Interval uses 00h/0Bh seconds only. Reject 2Ch/2Dh, milliseconds, unknown baseline, zero-as-default assumptions and any Project tolerance not explicitly approved.

Setting 0Bh does not itself prove timing. The single interval stimulus is a separately confirmed Chassis Control power cycle and must show OFF, ON and OS Ready; no reset, BMC reset or AC pull substitutes for it.
Policy trials use 00h/06h and physical AC loss only. BMC cold reset is recorded solely as policy-persistence evidence; it does not satisfy AC-return or interval behavior.

A qualified operator owns cable/outlet identification, disconnect/reconnect and electrical safety. The agent may prompt and collect evidence but cannot claim the physical step or visual/power observation occurred without human/PDU evidence.

Every disruptive command and each of four AC trials receives action-specific confirmation. No automatic retry after timeout, ambiguous response, missing transition or incorrect power state; stop and recover from preserved state.

Restore BASE_INTERVAL and original policy once under the approved recovery plan. Do not add an unplanned cycle merely to make a failed restore look successful; any additional verification cycle needs new approval and remains separate evidence.
expected_evidence: Exact Source Key/variant; BMC/firmware/SUT, OOB endpoint, single-DUT AC feed/topology, human operator, tool/clock versions and distinct IB/policy Source Keys
BASE_INTERVAL provenance/readback, 0Bh support, TEST_INTERVAL seconds/tolerance, raw one-time 0Bh response and any non-volatile readback
Action-specific interval-cycle approval and synchronized chassis-control, physical power OFF, power ON, POST, OS Ready and host/device/filesystem health timeline

Original policy, 06h support mask, current policy bits and for each of four trials: exact set, cold-reset/reconnect, persisted bits, starting host state, operator AC removal/return and expected final state
Human/PDU proof of correct outlet and de-energization, no shared-feed impact, preserved SEL/BMC/OS logs and explicit separation of BMC reset, chassis cycle and AC cycle
Restored BASE_INTERVAL and original policy plus final OS/monitoring health, PASS/FAIL/NOT READY/N/A by lane, uncovered coverage statement and confirmation that this review ran no DUT action
test_case.recovery: If the 0Bh write is ambiguous, do not resend; use the approved vendor readback or quarantine the setting until owner recovery. If the authorized chassis cycle does not show OFF, ON or OS Ready within its bounds, do not repeat: use the independent console/PDU to reach the approved safe state, preserve the timeline and restore BASE_INTERVAL once only after BMC stability. During a policy trial, an ambiguous 06h result is checked with read-only status; an incorrect AC-return outcome is stabilized manually without another AC pull. If BMC is unreachable after cold reset or AC return, keep the feed in the electrically safe state and invoke the independent recovery owner. Restore the original policy and interval only from known authoritative values; unknown or failed restoration quarantines the SUT and is FAIL, never a reason to reset, cycle or retry automatically.
test_case.manual_activity: A qualified operator verifies the dedicated feed, performs each physical AC disconnect/reconnect, witnesses de-energization and recovery, and owns electrical/host recovery. Automation is limited to preapproved OOB configuration, bounded status collection and evidence correlation.

source_conflict.reason: The immutable Master still names Power Cycle Interval while Procedure/Criteria duplicate Power Restore Policy, and DeepSeek supplies a third invalid 2Ch command. The Review layer preserves this conflict and requires both official lanes; it does not rewrite the source.

blocked.reason: IPMI 2.0 defines both operations and their separation. A conservative two-lane procedure preserves all coverage, while baselines, optional support, timing tolerance, feed mapping and approvals are bounded Project execution prerequisites rather than unknown core semantics.

external_authorities.title: Intelligent Platform Management Interface Specification v2.0 rev. 1.1 E7
external_authorities.application: Sections 28.2, 28.3, 28.8 and 28.9 plus Tables 28-3, 28-4, 28-9 and 28-10 define Chassis Status/Control, non-volatile restore-policy values/support, optional non-volatile 0Bh power-cycle interval in seconds and 00h no-delay semantics.

project_authority: The platform/power owner supplies the authoritative interval baseline/readback and tolerance, proves optional command support, selects the isolated feed and four policy trials, approves every disruptive transition and owns recovery. The owner cannot treat 2Ch, command completion, BMC reset, AC loss or the adjacent policy row as equivalent interval evidence, cannot waive the physical/manual evidence, and cannot merge distinct Source Keys.
